docs.title: Procedural CAD Gems
docs.text: Welcome to a gallery of parametric 3D models where code meets engineering and art. Each model in this collection is "baked" from Python scripts using the CadQuery framework.

docs.title: 🏛️ Architecture & Heritage
docs.text:
• Taj Mahal --- A grand procedural recreation of the iconic landmark, showcasing complex assembly and onion dome geometry. Explore Model

  • Byzantine Basilica --- A structural study of central-plan church architecture with hierarchical domes and arches. Explore Model

  • Ornate Facade --- A parametric study of decorative architectural elements and repetitive facade patterns. Explore Model

  • Onion Dome --- A mathematically derived 3D surface modelling the lobed dome of Saint Basil's Cathedral Explore Model

docs.title: 🧬 Science & Mathematics
docs.text:
• DNA Double Helix --- A biological masterpiece featuring color-coded base pairs and precise helical geometry. Explore Model

  • Trefoil Knot --- A topological wonder defined by a single continuous (2,3)-torus knot spline. Explore Model

  • Hyperboloid Lattice --- A demonstration of doubly ruled surfaces, combining structural efficiency with mathematical beauty. Explore Model

  • Platonic Solids: The Dodecahedron --- The dodecahedron is one of the five Platonic solids, a regular polyhedron with twelve equal pentagonal faces Explore Model

  • Platonic Solids: The Icosahedron --- The Icosahedron is the water element among the Platonic solids, featuring 20 equilateral triangular faces Explore Model

  • Small Stellated Dodecahedron --- Moving beyond the Platonic solids, these "Star Polyhedra" are non-convex regular solids discovered by Johannes Kepler Explore Model

  • Great Stellated Dodecahedron --- Moving beyond the Platonic solids, these "Star Polyhedra" are non-convex regular solids discovered by Johannes Kepler Explore Model

  • Disco Ball --- A study of multifaceted spherical surfaces and complex light reflection. Explore Model

docs.title: 🛠️ Engineering & Objects
docs.text:
• High-Voltage Tower --- A procedural lattice structure based on standard industrial blueprints (U35-type). Explore Model

  • Faceted Glass --- The "Soviet Classic" industrial design, featuring parametric facets and a tapered body. Explore Model

  • 🫖 The Royal Teapot --- The Royal Teapot (A Study in Classical Curves) Explore Model

  • Spiral Staircase --- A functional parametric assembly where step count and rotation are fully adjustable. Explore Model

docs.title: 🎨 Artistic Experiments
docs.text:
• Voronoi Shattered Text --- A simulation of structural decay using Voronoi partitioning on a 3D volume. Explore Model

  • Parametric Umbrella --- A combination of smooth revolved surfaces and structural support logic. Explore Model

  • ✏️ The Parametric Pencil --- A masterclass in "Digital Lathe" modeling. Unlike standard geometric approximations, this pencil is constructed through a multi-layered assembly (Skin, Body, Coal) and then "sharpened" using a dedicated tool object. Explore Model

  • 🍷Crystal Wineglass --- A sophisticated study in complex surface detailing using helical intersections. Explore Model

  • 💎 Wineglass v2 --- Procedural Goblet with Parabolic Stem Explore Model

  • 💎 Parametric Diamond-Cut Ellipsoidal Vase --- A sophisticated exploration of complex surface texturing on organic forms. This model transcends basic geometric primitives by utilizing an ellipsoid of revolution as its base body. Explore Model

  • 💎 Parametric Diamond-Cut Spline Vase Explore Model

  • 💎 Parametric Candy Bowl Explore Model

Unlike traditional CAD software where you draw with a mouse, every object in this collection is "baked" from Python scripts using the CadQuery framework. Instead of static files, these are living algorithms that can generate infinite variations of a design just by changing a few variables.

docs.title: Why Procedural CAD?
docs.text:
• Precision through Logic: Geometry is defined by mathematical relationships, ensuring perfect symmetry and alignment (e.g., in the Hyperboloid Lattice).
  • Infinite Scalability: Need a staircase with 10 steps or 100? Just update the n_steps parameter and the model rebuilds itself instantly.
  • Algorithmic Creativity: Some shapes, like the Voronoi Shattered Cube, would be nearly impossible to model manually, but are simple for a well-written script.
  • Version Control Ready: Since these models are code, they can be tracked, branched, and improved using Git, just like any other software project.

docs.title: How to Explore
docs.text:
1. Each model page includes:
  2. Interactive 3D Preview: Powered by , allowing you to inspect the geometry, shadows, and reflections directly in your browser.
  3. Technical Description: A breakdown of the engineering logic behind the model.
  4. Feel free to use the Camera icon in the 3D viewer to take high-quality snapshots of the models for your own use.
  5. Source Code: A link to the original Python script on GitHub so you can run it, modify it, and use it in your own projects. source.

docs.title: Parametric Byzantine Basilica
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A structural study of a central-plan church, characteristic of Byzantine and early Orthodox architecture. This model focuses on the "cross-in-square" geometry, where multiple semi-domes (apses) support and surround a central grand dome. It showcases how to use symmetry and repetition to build a complex, harmonious architectural volume.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Hierarchical Domes: A central dome positioned on a square base, flanked by four semi-domes (conches).
  • Procedural Arches: Windows and entrances are generated through automated boolean subtractions on the facade.
  • Classical Proportions: The relationship between the heights of the walls, drums, and domes is parametrically linked to maintain architectural balance.
  • Pure Geometry: Built entirely from primitives (spheres, boxes, cylinders), demonstrating clean CSG (Constructive Solid Geometry) principles.

docs.title: Dimensions
docs.text:
• Central Dome Radius: 10 mm
  • Total Height: 31 mm
  • Footprint: 50 x 50 mm

docs.title: Candy Bowl — Parametric Decorative Vessel in CadQuery
docs.text:
A fully parametric decorative bowl modelled entirely in code using CadQuery. The geometry, surface patterns, and ornamental cuts are all derived analytically — no mesh sculpting, no GUI modelling tools.

source

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This script builds a decorative candy bowl with a spherical body, a scalloped rim, and five distinct ornamental patterns cut into the surface. Every geometric decision — the wave profile of the rim, the diamond facets, the helical grooves — is expressed as a mathematical formula and applied through CadQuery's solid modelling kernel (OCCT).

The result is exported as a GLB file ready for 3D printing or rendering.

docs.title: 1. Base body
docs.text: The bowl starts as a unit sphere, clipped by two horizontal cutting planes to produce an open hemispherical cup with a flat bottom. A shell operation (shell(-w)) hollows the body to a uniform wall thickness w = 0.09.

docs.title: 2. Scalloped rim — fn_wave()
docs.text:
The rim is not a plain circle. A sinusoidal wave function

z = d · sin(α · n)

is sampled around the perimeter to generate a closed spline with n = 6 lobes. A circular profile is lofted along this path and subtracted from the shell, leaving a rhythmically scalloped upper edge. The amplitude d = 0.15 and lobe count are fully parametric.

docs.title: 3. Surface patterns
docs.text: Five independent ornamental patterns are cut into the sphere surface as Boolean subtractions.

docs.title: pattern0 — flat diamond ring
docs.text: A single lens-shaped groove (diamond_disc) is drawn between two points on a horizontal circle, then rotated nn = 19 times around the vertical axis to form a continuous decorative band near the base. The groove cross-section is the intersection of two spheres, giving a smooth concave profile.

docs.title: pattern1 — polar cap cluster
docs.text: Nine diamond_disc grooves are arranged on a small polar cap near the top of the bowl, forming a star-like incised rosette. The whole cluster is rotated to align with the rim lobes and then repeated n2 = 6 times around the axis.

docs.title: pattern2 — skew-chord ring
docs.text: Similar to pattern0 but placed on a tighter latitude circle with a skip of ns = 5 steps between chord endpoints, producing a star polygon outline. The assembly is tilted and repeated to interleave with pattern1.

docs.title: pattern3 — helical diamond grooves
docs.text:
diamond_line() sweeps a square cross-section along a parametric helix whose radial offset oscillates with a cubic ease-out term near the bottom. Two mirror-image helices (clockwise and counter-clockwise) are cut simultaneously, producing a crossed lattice of raised diamond ridges running from the base up the body.

d = (t - 0.5)*2
d = d*d*deep/2 + k*(1-t)**3 * deep

The cubic term k·(1−t)³ gently flares the groove outward at the base so the ridges fade smoothly into the flat bottom zone rather than terminating abruptly.

docs.title: pattern4 — latitude ring stack
docs.text: Seven horizontal ring grooves are cut at decreasing latitudes near the top, each with slightly decreasing depth and angular width. Together they form a series of concentric incised rings that frame the scalloped rim.

docs.title: Key techniques
docs.text:
diamond_disc(a, b, norm, d, alf) — the core primitive. Given two endpoints and a surface normal, it constructs a lens groove as the intersection of two offset spheres. The depth ratio d and opening angle alf control the sharpness of the cut. Used by pattern0, pattern1, and pattern2.

diamond_line(sol, h0, h1, alf_shift, deep) — sweeps a diamond-section profile along a parametric helix, using ray-casting (sol.intersect(line)) to pin each point to the actual surface of the solid. This means the groove follows the sphere's curvature exactly regardless of the helix parameters.

multi_disc() / multi_disc_comp() — rotational repetition helpers. multi_disc fuses copies into a single solid for Boolean cutting; multi_disc_comp returns a Compound for lighter preview. The distinction matters for performance with many copies.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Value Effect r 1.0 Bowl radius h 0.9 Height of cut from bottom h0 0.4 Height of cut from top w 0.09 Wall thickness n 6 Rim lobe count / rotational symmetry d 0.15 Rim wave amplitude hp0, hp1 −0.89, 0.3 Helix groove vertical extent

docs.title: Stack
docs.text: Library Role CadQuery Solid modelling, Boolean operations, shell, fillet OCCT (via CadQuery) Geometry kernel NumPy Vector maths for normals and chord geometry ocp-vscode In-editor preview

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
pip install cadquery ocp-vscode numpy

python CadQuery/candy_bowl.py
# exports ./stl/candy_bowl.glb

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
All five surface patterns share a single geometric primitive — the lens-shaped diamond_disc — but vary in placement, orientation, and repetition count to produce visually distinct decorations. Keeping one reusable primitive makes it straightforward to add new pattern bands or change symmetry without rewriting the cutting logic.

The helical grooves in pattern3 use live ray-casting against the current solid to position each path point. This couples the groove geometry to the bowl's actual surface, so the pattern automatically adapts if the sphere radius or clip heights are changed.

docs.text: Part of CadQueryScripts — a collection of parametric geometry experiments in Python.

docs.title: Voronoi Fragmentation Generator (Shattered Geometry)
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An algorithmic tool for breaking down any solid object into unique, interlocking shards using 3D Voronoi partitioning. This model showcases a "shattered" effect where a base volume is intersected with randomly generated Voronoi cells. It is perfect for procedural destruction effects, architectural puzzles, or artistic "exploded" views in web applications.

docs.title: Key Features:
docs.text:
1. Randomized Sharding: Uses a point-cloud seed to generate unique fracture patterns every time the script runs.
  2. Boolean Intersections: Leverages CadQuery’s robust kernel to create clean, sharp edges between shards.
  3. Individual Shard Control: Every fragment is an independent solid, allowing for individual animation or removal (e.g., "throwing away 40% of pieces").
  4. Customizable Complexity: Easily scale from a few large chunks to hundreds of tiny splinters.

docs.title: Dimensions
docs.text:
Bounding Box: (calculated from a string of text)

Shard Density: Variable (Controlled by the number of seed points)

docs.title: Procedural Disco Ball (Mirror Ball)
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A mathematically generated disco ball consisting of multiple flat rectangular facets mapped onto a spherical surface. This model demonstrates the power of coordinate transformation in CadQuery, where simple 2D tiles are precisely positioned in 3D space to form a perfectly faceted sphere. Ideal for testing PBR (Physically Based Rendering) materials and environment reflections.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
1. Adjustable Facet Density: Control the number of mirrors by changing the longitudinal and latitudinal segments.
  2. Perfect Spherical Mapping: Facets are calculated to maintain a consistent gapless structure.
  3. Rendering Optimized: Each facet is a flat surface, maximizing the "glitter" effect when used with environment maps (HDRI).
  4. Manifold Geometry: Despite having many faces, the model is a clean, watertight solid.

docs.title: Dimensions (Default)
docs.text:
Radius: 40 mm

Facet Count: 20 X 13 individual faces

docs.title: Parametric DNA Double Helix Generator
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A procedurally generated model of the Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA) double helix. This script demonstrates the power of parametric curves and polar coordinates in CadQuery. The model represents the classical B-DNA structure, featuring two intertwining sugar-phosphate backbones connected by color-coded nitrogenous base pairs. It’s an excellent educational tool for visualizing molecular biology through the lens of algorithmic design.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Dual-Helix Geometry: The backbones are generated using three-dimensional parametric splines defined by sine and cosine functions:
\[x = r \cdot \cos(\theta), \quad y = r \cdot \sin(\theta), \quad z = p \cdot \theta\]

  • Color-Coded Base Pairs: Features a visual representation of adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine (A-T, C-G) using distinct colors for the spheres and rungs.

  • Modular Assembly: Each segment of the strand (backbone, base, and hydrogen bond) is an independent object, allowing for easy adjustment of thickness and scale.

  • Periodic Repetition: The script can generate any number of "turns" (periods) of the helix by simply adjusting the total rotation parameter.

docs.title: Dimensions (Default)
docs.text:
• Helix Radius: 10 mm
  • Pitch (Height per turn): 34 mm
  • Base Pair Diameter: 2 mm
  • Sphere Radius: 3 mm

docs.title: Platonic Solids: The Dodecahedron
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The dodecahedron is one of the five Platonic solids, a regular polyhedron with twelve equal pentagonal faces. Historically, it was associated by Plato with the "fifth element" or the quintessence of the universe. In procedural CAD, it represents a classic challenge: calculating the precise dihedral angles and spatial rotations required to close the volume perfectly.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Golden Ratio Symbiosis: The coordinates of the vertices and the geometry of the pentagonal faces are intrinsically linked to the Golden Ratio (\(\phi \approx 1.618\)).

  • Algorithmic Precision: Unlike manual modeling, this script uses exact dihedral angles (\(\arccos(-1/\sqrt{5}) \approx 116.57^\circ\)) to align the faces, ensuring a 100% watertight manifold solid.

  • Spherical Symmetry: All 20 vertices lie perfectly on a circumscribed sphere, making it a masterpiece of balanced 3D geometry.

  • Versatile Base: The script can be easily extended to create hollow frames, "polyhedral dice" for gaming, or complex architectural hubs.

Mathematical Note (MathJax):The coordinates of the vertices of a regular dodecahedron with edge length \(2/\phi\) are:

\[(0, \pm 1, \pm \phi), \quad (\pm 1, \pm \phi, 0), \quad (\pm \phi, 0, \pm 1), \quad (\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1)\]

where \(\phi = \frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\) is the golden ratio.

docs.title: Dimensions (Default)
docs.text:
• Edge Length: \(L\)
  • Number of Faces: 12 (Regular Pentagons)
  • Dihedral Angle: \(\approx 116.57^\circ\)

docs.title: Parametric Hyperboloid Lattice (Ruled Surface)
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A stunning geometric structure based on a hyperboloid of one sheet. This model demonstrates how a complex curved surface can be created using only straight lines (rods). It is a "ruled surface," where every point on the surface belongs to at least one straight line. This principle allows for the creation of incredibly strong and lightweight architectural structures like the famous Shukhov Tower.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Ruled Surface Geometry: The lattice is generated by rotating straight lines at a specific angle, following the mathematical formula:
\[\frac{x^2 + y^2}{a^2} - \frac{z^2}{c^2} = 1\]
  • Dynamic Density: Easily adjust the number of intersecting rods to create either a dense mesh or a light, airy frame.
  • Structural Parameters: Control the top/bottom radii and the "waist" diameter to change the curvature of the tower.Circular Support Rings: Includes top and bottom reinforcing rings for a complete structural look.

docs.title: Dimensions (Default)
docs.text:
1. Base Radius: 50 mm
  2. Total Height: 120 mm
  3. Rod Diameter: 2 mm

docs.title: Platonic Solids: The Icosahedron
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Icosahedron is the water element among the Platonic solids, featuring 20 equilateral triangular faces. In CadQuery, this model is a study in high-order symmetry and structural optimization. It is the dual of the dodecahedron, meaning its vertices correspond to the centers of the dodecahedron's faces.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Maximum Volume Efficiency: Of all Platonic solids, the icosahedron has the largest volume for its surface area, making it a precursor to geodesic domes.

  • Golden Symmetry: Like the dodecahedron, its structure is dictated by the Golden Ratio (\(\phi\)).

  • Triangulated Rigidity: Ideal for structural space frames and complex architectural trusses.

Mathematical Note:The vertices of an icosahedron with edge length \(2\) are the cyclic permutations of:

\[(0, \pm 1, \pm \phi), \quad (\pm 1, \pm \phi, 0), \quad (\pm \phi, 0, \pm 1)\]

docs.title: Onion Dome — Parametric Surface Generator
docs.text:
A mathematically derived 3D surface modelling the lobed dome of Saint Basil's Cathedral. Built entirely in Python with NumPy, PyVista, and PIL — no 3D modelling software involved.

source

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This project generates a procedural onion-dome surface from scratch using pure mathematics. The geometry, mesh, and texture are each computed analytically — no hand-sculpting, no external assets.

The surface was independently derived to capture three architectural features of a Russian onion dome simultaneously:

  • the bulging profile that makes the dome wider than its base cylinder
  • the lobed segmentation into equal vertical panels
  • the helical twist of the ribs toward the apex

docs.title: 1. Surface geometry — onion.py
docs.text:
The surface is defined as a parametric function onion(u, v) over the unit square, mapping to (x, y, z) coordinates.

Profile and bulge (R(V)): the meridional radius uses a secant function to inflate the dome body beyond a cylindrical baseline. Below the inflection angle p = 90° + 35°, the radius stays constant; above it, R = 1 / cos(V − p), producing the characteristic outward swell.

Lobe geometry: the u parameter is scaled by n_lobes and split into integer (lobe index I) and fractional (local angle U) parts. Each lobe is a small circle of radius r_small = r_big · sin(π / n_lobes) rolling inside the full equatorial circle — giving n equal convex panels that meet cleanly at shared edges.

Twist: the rotation of each lobe around the vertical axis includes a twist term (cos(V) + 1) / 4 · π, which smoothly interpolates from zero twist at the equator to π/4 at the apex. This is what makes the ribs appear to spiral as they converge at the tip.

def onion(u, v, n_lobes=10):
    uu = u * n_lobes
    I  = np.floor(uu)
    U  = (uu - I) * math.pi - math.pi / 2
    V  = v * math.pi

    p      = np.pi / 2 + 35 / 180 * np.pi
    R      = np.where(V > p, 1.0 / np.cos(V - p), 1.0)
    z      = -R * np.cos(V)
    r_big  = np.abs(R * np.sin(V))

    twist   = (np.cos(V) + 1) / 4 * np.pi
    al      = 2 * np.pi / n_lobes
    r_small = r_big * np.sin(al / 2)

    _x = r_small * np.cos(U) + r_big * np.cos(al / 2)
    _y = r_small * np.sin(U)

    angle = al * I + twist
    x = _x * np.cos(angle) - _y * np.sin(angle)
    y = _x * np.sin(angle) + _y * np.cos(angle)
    return x, y, z

docs.title: 2. Mesh construction — surfgeometry.py
docs.text:
surf_geom() evaluates the parametric function on a regular (u, v) grid and assembles a PyVista StructuredGrid. Key features:

  • vectorised evaluation via np.meshgrid — no Python loops
  • optional polygon caps for top and bottom edges (top bitmask)
  • automatic UV texture coordinates with configurable tiling (repeat_u, repeat_v)
  • smooth per-point normals via compute_normals()
  • to_trimesh() / check_volume() helpers for watertightness validation before export

docs.title: 3. Procedural texture — Textures/lines.py
docs.text:
source

The stripe texture is generated entirely in NumPy — no image editor involved. A 1024 × 1024 grayscale map is built using a smoothstep function applied to a scaled x-coordinate, producing anti-aliased alternating bands. The sign term flips the gradient direction on every other stripe, creating the light/dark contrast visible on the render.

def smoothstep(edge0, edge1, x):
    t = np.clip((x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0), 0.0, 1.0)
    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)

The result is saved as a PNG and applied as a repeating texture in PyVista with smooth_shading=True.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text: Library Role NumPy Vectorised surface math, texture generation PyVista Mesh construction, UV mapping, rendering PIL / Pillow Texture export trimesh Mesh validation (watertightness check)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Effect n_lobes 10 Number of vertical dome panels p 125° Inflection angle controlling bulge onset res_u 500 Mesh resolution along u (circumference) res_v 50 Mesh resolution along v (height) nn (texture) 10 Number of texture stripes

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
pip install numpy pyvista pillow trimesh svgpathtools

# Generate texture first
python Textures/lines.py

# Render the dome
python PararmGeometry/onion.py

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text: The surface formula was derived independently to satisfy three geometric constraints at once: a smooth closed profile, equal-width lobes with no gaps or overlaps, and a twist that vanishes at the equator and reaches maximum at the apex. The smoothstep-based texture was written from scratch to avoid any dependency on image-editing software and to keep the stripe edges visually sharp at any resolution.

docs.title: ✏️ The Parametric Pencil
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A masterclass in "Digital Lathe" modeling. Unlike standard geometric approximations, this pencil is constructed through a multi-layered assembly (Skin, Body, Coal) and then "sharpened" using a dedicated tool object. This ensures that the transitions between the lacquer, the cedar wood, and the graphite core follow the exact laws of geometry seen in real-world objects.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Simulated Sharpening: The tip is generated by subtracting a conical pencil_sharpener solid from the hexagonal body, creating perfect hyperbolic intersections on each face.

  • Layered Anatomy: Features three distinct internal volumes:

    1. Coal (Lead): The central core.
    2. Body (Wood): The structural layer.
    3. Skin (Lacquer): The thin outer hexagonal shell.

  • Hexagonal Ergonomics: A standard hex-profile defined by the distance across flats, providing a classic drafting tool aesthetic.

docs.title: Technical Insight (Geometry):
docs.text:
The wavy edge where the hexagonal prism meets the sharpening cone is a result of the intersection of a plane and a cone. In 3D space, this intersection creates a hyperbolic curve on each of the six faces:

\[\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\]

docs.text: Moving beyond the Platonic solids, these "Star Polyhedra" are non-convex regular solids discovered by Johannes Kepler. These models represent the process of stellation—extending the faces of a regular dodecahedron until they intersect to form new, sharp vertices.

docs.title: Small Stellated Dodecahedron (small_dode)
docs.text:

docs.text:

  • Visual Style: A more aggressive, "shiky" version of the star, representing the final stage of dodecahedron stellation.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:

docs.title: Parametric Trefoil Knot (Mathematical Sculpture)
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Trefoil Knot is the simplest example of a non-trivial knot in topology. This model is a (2,3)-torus knot, meaning it winds around a torus (donut shape) twice in one direction and three times in the other. It is a continuous, self-intertwining loop that demonstrates how CadQuery can handle complex 3D paths and smooth sweeping operations.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Parametric Spline Path: The knot is generated using a set of parametric equations that define a seamless, periodic curve in 3D space:
\[x = \sin(t) + 2\sin(2t)\] \[y = \cos(t) - 2\cos(2t)\] \[z = -\sin(3t)\]

  • Sweep Geometry: The solid volume is created by sweeping a circular profile along the calculated spline, ensuring a constant cross-section throughout the entire loop.

  • Topological Perfection: The model is a single, manifold solid with no self-intersections, making it ideal for both mathematical visualization and 3D printing.

  • Adjustable Thickness: The diameter of the "rope" and the overall scale of the knot can be easily modified through script parameters.

  • Tube Diameter: 5 mm

docs.title: 💎 Parametric Diamond-Cut Ellipsoidal Vase
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A sophisticated exploration of complex surface texturing on organic forms. This model transcends basic geometric primitives by utilizing an ellipsoid of revolution as its base body. The primary challenge and achievement of this script lie in the precise mathematical mapping of a "diamond-cut" crystal pattern onto a surface with non-constant curvature.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Ellipsoidal Base Geometry: The vase profile is driven by an elliptical arc, creating a natural "swelling" form that provides more aesthetic depth than standard conical or cylindrical shapes.

  • Procedural Diamond Lattice: The intricate facets are generated through the boolean subtraction of mirrored helical sweeps. The script dynamically adjusts the cutting path to account for the changing radius of the ellipsoid, ensuring perfect facet alignment from the weighted base to the polished rim.

  • Optical Realism: Specifically designed for high-end PBR rendering, the geometry maximizes light refraction and internal "fire," mimicking the properties of heavy lead crystal.

  • Deep Parametric Control: Every dimension—from the ellipsoid’s major/minor axes to the density and depth of the helical grooves—is fully adjustable, allowing for a wide range of silhouettes (from tall bud vases to wide decorative bowls).

docs.title: Mathematical Insigh
docs.text:
To maintain a consistent cut depth on a curved surface, the tool-path radius \(r\) is calculated as a function of height \(z\) following the ellipsoidal equation:

\[\frac{x^2 + y^2}{a^2} + \frac{z^2}{b^2} = 1\]

This ensures that the "diamond" shapes remain undistorted even as the vase tapers towards the top and bottom.

docs.title: 🍷Crystal Wineglass
docs.text: source

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A sophisticated study in complex surface detailing using helical intersections. The model features a classic "diamond-cut" crystal pattern achieved by projecting and subtracting mirrored helical paths along a conical surface. This demonstrates advanced control over 3D paths in CadQuery, where the radius of the cutting tool evolves with the height of the glass.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Conical Helix Patterning: Procedural diamond facets generated through the intersection of left-handed and right-handed conical spirals.

  • Faceted Stem: A multi-stage stem transition that enhances light refraction and provides a tactile grip.

  • Optical Realism: Designed to maximize the "fire" of the crystal in PBR environments, showcasing complex internal reflections.

  • Variable Geometry: Every element—from the bowl's taper to the facet depth—is controlled by parameters, allowing for instant transformation from a shot glass to a flute.

docs.title: The Math of the Conical Helix
docs.text:
To map the lines correctly on a tapering bowl, the radius \(r\) must be a function of the height \(z\). If the cone has a half-angle \(\alpha\), the path follows:

\[x(\theta) = (R_{base} + z \cdot \tan \alpha) \cos(\theta)\] \[y(\theta) = (R_{base} + z \cdot \tan \alpha) \sin(\theta)\]
